content.text: ▪︎RF: uncircumcised, poor hygiene, DM (check glucose if recurrent)
▪︎HIV + obesity also ⇡risk of candidal; candidal balanitis may be the 1st presentation of DM
▪︎circinate balanitis: assoc w/ reactive arthritis; shallow ulcers on the glans
▪︎Candida (#1 infectious): erythema + satellite papules/pustules, white curd-like d/c, pruritus → topical azole
▪︎Bacterial: thick foul purulent exudate, edema → abx
: constricted foreskin cannot be retracted over the glans
: constricted foreskin = retracted over the glans & cannot be ↓
▪︎paraphimosis = medical emergency → ischemia + necrosis w/o immediate manual or surgical reduction
▪︎candidal: topical imidazole (clotrimazole, miconazole), nystatin cream, or PO fluconazole
▪︎bact: topical metronidazole, PO Augmentin, or clindamycin cream (anaerobe sus); mupirocin cream, PO dicloxacillin, or PO cephalexin (strep/staph sus)
▪︎proper hygiene + mgnt of underlying causes (DM, HIV, obesity)
⚠️ Blueprint picture: “distal foreskin” = posthitis only; purulent exudate = bacterial, not candidal
Prostate hyperplasia (periurethral or transitional zone) leading to bladder outlet obstruct
– hyperplasia = part of the norm aging process & = dep on ↑DHT prod
▪︎MC benign tumor in men; incidence ⇡ w/ age (MC >50–60yo)
▪︎stromal + epithelial cell growth in the transitional zone → prostatic urethral compression
▪︎assoc w/ DM, cold/sinus meds, OSA, insomnia, hematuria
: hesitancy, weak or intermittent stream force, incomplete emptying, & terminal dribbling
Sympathomimetics & anticholinergics may worsen the sxs
▪︎HI FUN: Hesitancy, Intermittence/incontinence, Frequency/fullness, Urgency, Nocturia
▪︎also ⇣force/caliber of stream, double voiding, straining to urinate, dysuria; some pts aSx
uniformly enlrg, firm, nontender, rubbery prostate
▪︎smooth, elastic; palpable median sulcus; ⍉nodules or induration (induration → exclude prostate CA)
: to look for hematuria or other cause of sxs
▪︎CT or kidney US only w/ UTI or comps (hematuria, CKD, hx of stones); urodynamics, uroflowmetry, PVR at clinician discretion
▪︎1st-line: reassurance + lifestyle (⇣fluids before bed, ⇣caffeine/EtOH, timed voiding); meds = mainstay
: best initial therapy to rapidly relieve sxs but do ⍉Δ prostate size
▪︎tamsulosin: α1a-selective → fewer systemic SEs (orthostatic ↓BP, dizziness, tiredness, rhinitis, HA); floppy iris syndrome (cataract surg)
: reduce the size of the prostate over 6-12mo
▪︎finasteride: blocks T → DHT; acts on epithelial component → ↓size + improves Sx; may ⇣ urinary retention + need for intervention (mod-severe Sx)
▪︎PDE-5-i (tadalafil): FDA-approved for BPH Sx ± ED; ⍉↓prostate size
▪︎anticholinergics: tolterodine, oxybutynin, darifenacin, solifenacin, fesoterodine, trospium
▪︎TURP: recurrent UTIs, hematuria, azotemia, bladder stones, or Sx that interfere w/ QOL
▪︎stress: urethral hypermobility or intrinsic sphincter deficiency (childbirth, menopause/urethral atrophy, aging, obesity, prostate surg) → leakage when ⇡intra-abd P > urethral resistance
▪︎urge: detrusor overactivity → involuntary bladder contractions during filling; idiopathic MCC
▪︎overflow: impaired detrusor contractility (DM, MS, SCI) or bladder outlet obstruction (BPH, POP) → incomplete emptying + overdistended bladder
▪︎stress: leakage w/ cough, sneeze, laugh, or lifting; ⍉urge beforehand
▪︎urge: sudden, strong urge → leakage before reaching the bathroom; ⇡freq, nocturia
▪︎overflow: frequent dribbling w/o urge or trigger; weak stream, incomplete emptying
▪︎stress: urine leak w/ cough on exam (cough stress test); nml PVR
▪︎stress: PFMT (Kegel), pessary; surg: midurethral sling or Burch
▪︎urge: bladder training (timed voiding), ⇣caffeine/EtOH, Kegel; antimuscarinics (oxybutynin) = 1st-line meds
▪︎overflow: intermittent cath; tx cause (eg BPH, POP)
▪︎mixed: PFMT (Kegel); antimuscarinic (oxybutynin) for the urge component
